entities.name: PMID:25082957
observations: Single-blind randomized controlled trial in 66 patients with Parkinson disease at Hoehn and Yahr stage 3.
Participants received 12 sessions of 45 minutes over 4 weeks of robot-assisted gait training or balance training.

Robot-assisted gait training used progressive gait-speed increases and decreasing body-weight support; balance training targeted postural reactions, destabilization, coordination, and locomotor dexterity.
Berg Balance Scale was the primary outcome; Activities-Specific Balance Confidence Scale, Timed Up and Go, and Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale were secondary outcomes.

No significant between-group differences were found immediately after treatment or at 1-month follow-up; authors concluded robot-assisted gait training was not superior to balance training for postural instability.

entities.name: Parkinson disease
observations: The trial enrolled patients at Hoehn and Yahr stage 3, characterized in the paper as mild to moderate Parkinson disease.

entities.name: Robot-assisted gait training
observations: Intervention consisted of 12 45-minute sessions over 4 weeks, with progressive gait-speed increases and decreasing body-weight support.

entities.name: Balance training
observations: Comparator consisted of 12 45-minute sessions over 4 weeks targeting postural reactions, self- and externally induced destabilization, coordination, and locomotor dexterity.

entities.name: No RAGT superiority
observations: Immediately after treatment, Berg Balance Scale scores were 51.58 ± 3.94 with robot-assisted gait training versus 51.15 ± 3.46 with balance training, with no significant between-group difference.
At 1-month follow-up, Berg Balance Scale scores were 51.03 ± 4.63 versus 50.97 ± 4.28, respectively, again with no significant between-group difference.
Secondary outcomes likewise showed no significant between-group differences.
